youtube.title: 1,200Gs: How Woodpeckers Don't Die #shorts

instagram.caption:
1,200Gs of force per peck—your brain would turn to soup, theirs has a shock absorber.

Woodpeckers peck 20 times per second without brain damage. Their skulls contain spongy bone that absorbs impact and redirects force away from neural tissue. Scientists study this adaptation to prevent human traumatic brain injury.

If humans evolved this bone structure tomorrow, how much harder could our athletes hit?
